name: Speaker-twin Monte Carlo for mention markets (scripted speakers, maker expression)
one_line: Simulate a scripted speaker's earnings call, Fed press conference or briefing a few hundred times, count strike words under the contract rule, blend with a transcript base rate and the price, and rest maker quotes where they disagree; the NO-side ladder is file 23's.
maturity: Experimental; no synthetic-transcript forecaster scored against a price anywhere; the one paper (Kim et al.) asks for a probability, LLM 0.1470 vs market 0.1402, blend 0.1392; the only live base-rate/LLM record lost $16.40 on 1,115 bets
requires_ai: yes; LLM writes synthetic remarks and analyst/reporter Q&A twins
edge: Hypothetical: agenda-conditioned word counts that frequency base rates and retail miss
capital: <$1k to test; a few $k to trade, capacity-bound ($16-64 near touch per strike)
build_time: 3-5 weeks solo for Fed and briefings; +2-3 weeks and a transcript licence for earnings calls
opportunity_size: Polymarket scripted strikes shrinking: earnings $145k in Sep 2026 (13 events), Warsh pressers $143-311k; Kalshi 10-30x larger in contracts
expected_results: no public data, theoretical only; guess 0-0.003 Brier over the price, net negative after LLM spend
competition: no twin trader found; retail YES buyers, NO sellers, maker walls, live snipers
flag: grey; script-holder insiders (Perez), CFTC mention review, impersonation, copyright
validate: Leak-controlled replay at T-24h, six arms; kill if twin + base rate = base rate + market
top_risk: Price already beats base rates; the twin adds nothing measurable
solo_fit_reason: The Fed and briefing pipeline is buildable on free transcripts, but on 2,597 resolved scripted strikes the price beats every base rate tested (0.152 vs 0.246 at T-24h), the best transcript-base blend gains 0.0018 on Fed pressers, near-touch depth is $16-64 a strike and LLM spend per event rivals it; the only structural profit (NO on 20-50c) is file 23's, needs no twin, and at executed prices survives only on small tickets (+8.9c per strike, -0.4c size-weighted).
speed_class: speed-insensitive: one rollout batch at T-24h; price flat to T-1h
results_10k: not as sized; -$780 to +$90/month, capital idles (guess)
min_capital: $0 until Phase 1 passes; ~$1-2k after, for per-event caps
capacity_ceiling: ~$3-5k resting across a month's scripted strikes
services: Polymarket Gamma API (mention series, rules, startTime)
monthly_running_cost: minimum ~$30-60; comfortable ~$400-900 plus an earnings-transcript licence
changes_made: Written 2026-09-29 with live checks: Gamma census of 1,238 closed mention events and the 193 scripted-speaker events (135 earnings calls, 18 Fed-chair, 40 briefings; 3,037 resolved strikes), rules text per class (earnings 'mentioned by anyone', Fed 'if Warsh says', briefings 'acting Press Secretary'), volume by half-year and month; CLOB prices-history (10-minute grid, window start-3d to start+1h) for 2,597 strikes in 163 events at T-24h / T-6h / T-1h from the scheduled start, strikes counted only if listed by then; leave-future-out hierarchical Beta-Binomial (and a term-pooled variant) and a leave-future-out blend; YES rate by price band and NO on 20-50c at executable prices; event-clustered bootstrap CIs; power from the per-event SD.

Fed-chair sub-study: 30 FOMC press-conference transcripts (federalreserve.gov, 2023-2026) parsed to chair-only turns; rule parser reproduces 316 of 320 Polymarket resolutions; start times taken from the Fed schedule because Gamma startTime is an hour off on 5 of 15 events and the 'May 2025' event carries the March date; transcript base rate (previous eight transcripts) 0.204 vs market 0.179 at T-24h, blend gain 0.0018 [0.0000, 0.0040], none at T-1h.

Live books on the Micron and Nike calls (median 35c spread, $64 YES bids and $16 to buy NO within 5c); Kalshi mention series and markets (191 earnings series, 101 events July-September 2026 at a median 90,758 contracts; Fed pressers 1.07M and 0.75M contracts; Kalshi earnings rule counts only company representatives).

Adjacent sources fetched: Kim et al. 2602.21229 (probability prompt, not transcript generation; 7 days out; alpha on held-out split; no CI), the Beck detector README (-$16.40; Beta-Binomial scorer -$13.37 on 132 bets), McInerney (NO ladder, self-reported), two DeFi Rate pages, Polymarket fee docs, arXiv abstracts 2407.12855, 2411.18382, 2507.16799, 2509.19088, 2510.14205, 2508.13635, 2512.23847, 2511.15214; GitHub and HN searches.

Critic note applied: the twin is labelled Experimental; the NO-side ladder is routed to file 23 and its scripted-speaker confirmation (+11.6c at the mid, +5.7c after a 5c half-spread) is reported as file 23's rule, not this file's edge.

Cite-check + skeptic pass 2026-09-29 (22 numbered sources re-fetched or re-queried: 9 arXiv abstracts via the export API, Kim et al. HTML, the Beck README, McInerney, both DeFi Rate pages, Polymarket fee docs, Fortune, Gamma rule texts, Kalshi API, three Fed transcript PDFs, GitHub API; E7 / E8 / E9 passages checked; 19 confirmed, 3 corrected, 0 removed, 0 unreachable; analyse.py and fed_analyse.py outputs reproduced): (1) `prices-history` is the raw book midpoint (equals CLOB /midpoint on 24 of 24 live strikes, e.g. 0.605 on a 0.26/0.95 book), so the +11.6c NO result is a mid figure; re-priced on 54,606 executed taker fills (Data API v1 /trades, takerOnly=true) the resting NO seller earned +8.9c per strike [5.1, 12.4] but -0.4c size-weighted [-7.6, +11.1] (fills from 100-1,000-share orders, 59% of shares, lost ~4c), +4.7c capped at 20 shares; taker NO buyers +4.9c per strike; NO-side maker capital filled per event median $363; credited to file 23 as a small-ticket rent; (2) timing audit: Gamma startTime is an hour EARLY on 6 (not 5) of 15 Fed pressers, so the main sample's T-1h is not contaminated there; DraftKings Nov 2025 rule text gave the wrong time (10 of 13 strikes decided at T-6h); briefing start times are hindsight anchors; (3) power split: base-rate-scale disagreement needs ~390 events / ~120 pressers for 0.01, but the blend-vs-blend pass test (Fed SD 0.068 per event) needs ~18 pressers for 0.002 and ~72 for 0.001; (4) corrections: CFTC quote (NPR 'taking a hard look'; 'particularly susceptible' is the rule's category language), briefing peak $273k (not $176k), Warsh median strike $4.0k (not $5.8k), Kalshi contracts vs dollars caveat, Coinbase call ~$4k on Polymarket vs $80,933 on Kalshi, Gao et al. task = capex from earnings-call transcripts, 13 of 3,037 strikes with a dispute round, 1,708 strikes predate fees; Fed disagreement rule negative at half today's 35c spread; Data API /trades added to services; 15 fields 2,722 -> ~2,550 words.
open_doubts: Historical books are not recoverable: the executed-fill test shows what takers paid, not whether a new resting order would have been filled ahead of the queue; size-weighted maker PnL is ~0 and every capped variant's interval spans zero.
The earnings-call base rate uses only Polymarket's own resolved history; a transcript-frequency base rate needs licensed transcripts and may come much closer to the price on earnings calls.
Briefing horizons are anchored on start times set after the briefing was scheduled; a live pipeline would often not know T-24h for a briefing.
The Fed disagreement rule (+13.9c at the mid, +8.2c after a 5c half-spread) is one of several cells on 15 events, vanishes at T-1h and is negative at half today's spread: a hypothesis for file 23.
No twin was run; cost per event ($2-35 on batch) and the agenda-noun over-count rest on list prices and one pre-2025 stylometry paper; the blend-vs-blend power figure rests on 10 Fed events.
